findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization branch renders hard-coded empty data instead of query results
findings.body: In tableResultComponent, when organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization') is true, the code renders <TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} /> instead of passing the actual `result`/`fields`/`metadata` that are available in this scope (and which are passed to the StyledSimpleTableChart in the other branch). As written, enabling this feature flag will always render an empty table regardless of the real query results, making table widgets effectively broken for any organization with the flag on.

findings.title: validate_timestamp/validate_age use truthy checks instead of presence checks
findings.body: BrowserReportSerializer.validate_timestamp checks `self.initial_data.get("age")` and validate_age checks `self.initial_data.get("timestamp")` to enforce that exactly one of the two fields is present. Since both checks rely on truthiness rather than key presence, a report containing `timestamp=0` together with `age=0` (or vice versa) will bypass the mutual-exclusivity validation entirely, because `0` is falsy. This silently accepts malformed/ambiguous reports that the validators are supposed to reject, and there is no test covering the zero-value edge case.

findings.title: Overly broad exception handling and non-serializable value in log extra
findings.body: get_environment_info wraps the whole body in `except Exception as e` and logs at `logger.info` with `extra={"issue_id": issue.id, "error": e}`. Catching all exceptions this broadly (not just the expected Environment.DoesNotExist / missing-event cases) will silently swallow genuine bugs (e.g. AttributeError from a code defect, DB errors) and mislabel them as the benign 'no environment' case at info level, making real failures hard to notice. Additionally, putting the raw exception object `e` (rather than str(e) or using exc_info) into the `extra` dict can fail to serialize cleanly depending on the logging backend/formatter in use.

findings.title: Caching/retry safeguards lost when switching from useApiQuery to raw useQuery
findings.body: The previous implementation called useApiQuery with explicit `staleTime: 0, refetchOnWindowFocus: false, retry: false`. The refactor replaces this with a bare `useQuery({enabled, queryKey, queryFn})` that omits all three options, so the hook now falls back to the QueryClient's global defaults for staleness, window-focus refetching, and retries. This can introduce unwanted retries on failed attribute-key fetches and extra refetches whenever the browser tab regains focus, which the original code explicitly avoided — a behavior regression for a hook used in interactive search/typeahead UI.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline may be too tight for a 100-identity chunk doing network calls
findings.body: check_auth_identities now has `processing_deadline_duration=60` while it is invoked with `chunk_size=100` (the default) and loops over each auth identity calling `check_single_auth_identity`, which in turn calls `provider.refresh_identity(auth_identity)` — a network-bound call to the external SSO/auth provider for each identity. Giving only 60 seconds total to refresh up to 100 identities (effectively ~0.6s per identity including request overhead) risks the task being killed mid-batch under normal network latency, which would abort remaining identity refreshes in that chunk without obvious indication which ones were processed.

findings.title: Environment filter silently dropped from trace-item attribute key requests
findings.body: The previous implementation (in useTraceItemAttributeKeys.tsx) explicitly sent `environment: selection.environments` as part of the query to `/organizations/.../trace-items/attributes/`. The new shared `makeTraceItemAttributeKeysQueryOptions` omits the environment parameter entirely, with only a comment stating it's 'left out intentionally as it's not supported'. If the backend endpoint does in fact filter by environment, this is a behavior regression that will cause attribute-key suggestions to no longer respect the user's selected environment(s); this should be confirmed against the backend endpoint's actual support for the parameter.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before feature flag and input validation
findings.body: analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...) is called unconditionally at the very start of post(), before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any request validation. This means analytics will record an 'assemble' event even for requests that are ultimately rejected with 404 (feature disabled) or 400 (invalid payload), inflating/skewing usage metrics for this event rather than reflecting actual successful or attempted assemble operations.
